network.overall_strategy: This is a connected, literature-guided hypothesis network, not an experimentally established synthesis of free glutamine. The supplied literature supports several routes to glutamate and a cyanosulfidic route to its aminodinitrile precursor, but does not establish the decisive prebiotic glutamine-forming transformations. The ten pathways below are distinct conditional reaction sequences, not ten validated or independent syntheses. Eight combine four glutamate-supply routes with two explicitly speculative activation mechanisms; two investigate alternative orders of nitrile hydrolysis. The side-chain-first nitrile pathway is a low-priority hypothesis because the cited analogue chemistry does not support its required selectivity. No target yield, net accumulation, or high-confidence end-to-end feasibility is asserted. Boundary feedstocks include glyoxylate, pyruvate, hydroxylamine, acetyl phosphate and cyanamide; their production and environmental concentrations are not established by this graph. Reaction nodes describe balanced net transformations rather than every elementary step. Explicit coefficients appear in mechanism strings, while each molecule ID appears only once per input or output array. Neutral parent formulas are used for acid-base families except where charged species are needed for redox accounting. Unverified InChIs are null. Glutamine has the connectivity HOOC-CH(NH2)-CH2-CH2-CONH2, distinct from isoglutamine; no enantioselection is claimed. A molecule's environment_formed is representative when several environments produce it. The schema lacks a byproduct role, so terminal byproducts are classified as intermediate. Numerical settings identified as proposed screens are experimental-design parameters, not reported successful synthesis conditions. Modules require separate reactors or pools: copper-rich, sulfidic, nickel-rich, iron-rich and aluminium-rich streams are not assumed compatible. Cooling, settling and shaded transport are specified where relevant, but selective organic purification and quantitative transfer efficiencies remain unresolved. All glutamine-forming tests use cool, UV-shielded water at pH 5-7.5. Product identification must distinguish glutamine, isoglutamine, glutamate and pyroglutamate using authentic standards and non-hydrolytic analysis. Accumulation requires measured production to exceed cyclization, hydrolysis and transport losses.

reactions.name: Copper-mediated oxidative formation of cyanoacetylene
agents: Cu(I) chloride complexes as a catalytic seed in concentrated chloride brine

conditions.catalyst: Cu(I) chloride complexes; Cu(II) is a stoichiometric oxidant
conditions.other: Anoxic, sulfide-free compartment. Proposed screen: 10 mM HCN, 20 mM Cu(II), 1-10 mM Cu(I) seed and 1-3 M total chloride, with acetylene supplied from a gas phase; 0.5-24 h. These concentrations and residence times are not a reproduced Patel recipe. Separate copper-containing solids before sulfide exposure.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_001 + mol_002 + 2 mol_006 -> mol_009 + 2 mol_007 + 2 mol_008. Oxidative coupling includes copper-bound intermediates and subsequent liberation of cyanoacetylene; ligand speciation is not resolved.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) support Cu(II)-dependent coupling of HCN and acetylene. Copper(II) supplies the oxidizing equivalents here; molecular oxygen is neither an input nor an implied regeneration reagent. Sustained Cu(II) availability on an anoxic, Fe(II)-rich surface is an unresolved geochemical requirement. The cited work supports the transformation, not the proposed operating window or integration with downstream pools.

reactions.name: Hydrocyanation of cyanoacetylene to maleonitrile

conditions.other: Proposed 1-10 mM cyanoacetylene and comparable HCN, pH 7-8, 0.5-24 h, in a covered receiving pool. Copper carryover and competing cyanohydrin/aminonitrile production must be measured; no selective separation yield is assumed.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_009 + mol_001 -> mol_010. Cyanide addition to the activated alkyne followed by protonation produces the unsaturated dinitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) experimentally obtained maleonitrile from cyanoacetylene with HCN-containing mixtures. Their product distributions depend on pH and ammonia. This node represents the measured maleonitrile branch, not quantitative conversion of the entire mixture or an established environmental concentration.

reactions.name: Sulfide-driven photoreduction of the unsaturated dinitrile

conditions.pressure: Approximately 1 bar in an anoxic headspace
conditions.other: Proposed substrate 1-5 mM, total dissolved sulfide 5-20 mM, pH 7-8. Laboratory benchmark: 254 nm irradiation; proposed incident irradiance 0.1-1 mW/cm2 and sampling over 0.25-24 h. Solar-spectrum performance must be tested separately. Copper is not assumed necessary for this sulfide-reductant implementation.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced formal equation: 8 mol_010 + 8 mol_004 -> 8 mol_011 + mol_015. Photochemical electron transfer and protonation reduce the carbon-carbon double bond. S8 represents the ultimate elemental-sulfur redox endpoint, not a demonstrated exclusive immediate sulfur product.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) support photoreduction of the maleonitrile/fumaronitrile system to succinonitrile. Photoisomerization can accompany this net transformation. Their optimized step yield is not an integrated-network yield. Sulfide supply and irradiation under natural spectra remain constraints (Ranjan et al., 2018). No molecular oxygen is required.

reactions.name: Photoreductive conversion of one succinonitrile group to an aldehyde

conditions.other: Separate irradiation stage after rxn_003. Proposed 1-5 mM succinonitrile, 5-20 mM total sulfide, pH 7-8, 254 nm laboratory illumination at 0.1-1 mW/cm2, sampled over 0.25-24 h. End irradiation upon measured aldehyde production; no assumed residence-time optimum.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced formal equation: 8 mol_011 + 8 mol_004 + 8 mol_005 -> 8 mol_012 + 8 mol_003 + mol_015. Reduction of one nitrile to an imine-equivalent followed by hydrolysis gives 3-cyanopropanal and ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) support selective monoreduction of succinonitrile to the semialdehyde under their laboratory conditions. This selectivity concerns photoreduction of succinonitrile, not the later regioselective hydrolysis required for glutamine. Sulfur speciation, aldehyde lifetime and performance with realistic sunlight remain integration uncertainties.

reactions.name: Cyanohydrin formation from 3-cyanopropanal

conditions.other: Shaded receiving pool, proposed pH 7-9, 1-10 mM aldehyde and 1-3 equivalents total HCN; sample from minutes to 24 h. Transfer follows cessation of irradiation and settling of sulfur solids. Dissolved sulfide and metal carryover are not assumed absent.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_012 + mol_001 -> mol_013. Reversible nucleophilic addition of cyanide to the aldehyde, followed by protonation, forms the cyanohydrin.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) support cyanohydrin formation from this aldehyde precursor. The chemistry does not require a mineral catalyst. Product dilution, aldehyde side reactions and sequential HCN delivery remain environmental constraints rather than solved aspects of the network.

reactions.name: Strecker equilibration to the glutamate/glutamine aminodinitrile

conditions.other: Proposed 1-10 mM cyanohydrin, 0.1-1 M total ammonia/ammonium, pH 9-10, 1-72 h, protected from further UV. These are precursor-forming conditions, not glutamine-storage conditions. Volatilization and ammonia concentration must be assessed.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_013 + mol_003 -> mol_014 + mol_005. Cyanohydrin dissociation, aldehyde-imine equilibration and cyanide capture give the alpha-aminonitrile; this is not direct displacement of an unactivated hydroxyl group.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) obtained the aminodinitrile, reporting approximately 70% over the aldehyde-to-aminonitrile sequence. That value is not a glutamine yield. The paper did not establish subsequent selective hydrolysis to glutamine. Sequential delivery and the concentrated ammonia requirement remain unresolved environmental issues.

reactions.name: Candidate complete hydrolysis of the aminodinitrile to glutamate

conditions.other: Proposed 1-10 mM aminodinitrile in 0.1-1 M acid, sampled over 6-48 h. Quantify glutamate, lactams and unresolved products. Before any amidation test, cool shallow runoff to at most 303 K and neutralize by mineral-buffered mixing. Cooling, dilution, salts and organic recovery require measurement.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced parent-species equation: mol_014 + 4 mol_005 -> mol_020 + 2 mol_003. Both nitriles undergo hydration to amides followed by hydrolysis to carboxylic acids. Ammonia is predominantly ammonium under the actual acidic conditions.
reactions.reasoning: Complete nitrile hydrolysis is chemically conventional, but this substrate-specific prebiotic implementation is not demonstrated in the supplied studies and is therefore conditional. Patel et al. (2015) establish the precursor, not this conversion. Hot acid would destroy any glutamine already present, so this route supplies glutamate only. Carbon-skeleton recovery and subsequent delivery to cool activation water remain unvalidated.

reactions.name: Hydrogen-driven net assembly of alpha-ketoglutarate

conditions.temperature: 295-303 K; 295 K is the reported laboratory benchmark
conditions.other: Abiotic H2-retaining water-filled pore or laboratory analogue, not an enzymatic system. Proposed 5-20 mM each glyoxylate and pyruvate, pH 7-8, Ni powder 1-10 g/L, 1-72 h. Nickel loading and residence time are proposed, not extracted from the supplied report. Exclude sulfide-rich inflow because of catalyst poisoning.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_016 + mol_017 + mol_018 -> mol_019 + mol_005. Carbon-carbon bond formation, dehydration and hydrogenation are represented as one net reductive-aldol assembly module.
reactions.reasoning: Kaur et al. (2024) support H2/Ni-associated formation of alpha-ketoglutarate from smaller ketoacid precursors. This is the hydrogen-driven module, not the metal-free glyoxylate network of Stubbs et al. (2020). The proposed concentrations and catalyst loading require verification. A 5-bar H2 compartment is not an ambient-pressure surface pool, which is why the variable-condition Biochemical category is used.

reactions.name: Nickel-catalysed hydrogen-driven reductive amination

conditions.other: pH 7-8. Proposed 5 mM alpha-ketoglutarate, 150 mM total ammonia/ammonium and Ni powder 1-10 g/L; sample over 1-72 h. At pH 7.5 and pKa approximately 9.25, 150 mM total ammonia gives about 2.6 mM NH3. Settle or filter nickel solids before activation tests; dissolved metal carryover remains.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_019 + mol_003 + mol_018 -> mol_020 + mol_005. Carbonyl-ammonia condensation followed by nickel-mediated hydrogenation produces glutamate.
reactions.reasoning: Kaur et al. (2024) support reductive amination of alpha-ketoglutarate using H2, ammonia and nickel near room temperature. The supplied study summary gives 5 bar H2 and pH 7-8, but not the proposed nickel loading. Glutamate formation does not validate subsequent gamma-amidation. Alpha-ketoglutarate is not generically the fastest reductive-amination substrate (Mayer and Moran, 2022).

reactions.name: Iron-driven reduction of the alpha-ketoglutarate hydroxylamine adduct

conditions.pressure: Approximately 1 bar under an inert atmosphere
conditions.other: Proposed 5 mM alpha-ketoglutarate, 5-10 mM hydroxylamine, 25-100 mM Fe(0) as fine filings, pH 5-6 and 1-24 h. Exact pH and loading are proposed screens. Fe(0) is consumed, not treated as a catalyst. Cool to at most 303 K and remove metal solids before downstream testing; residual hydroxylamine must be measured.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced formal equation: mol_019 + mol_021 + 2 mol_022 + 4 mol_008 -> mol_020 + 2 mol_005 + 2 mol_023. Oxime formation is followed by four-electron reduction, with two Fe(0) atoms oxidized to Fe(II).
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. (2019) support iron/hydroxylamine amino-acid formation under inert conditions around 343 K. The equation explicitly accounts for the consumed metal and protons. The proposed recipe is not presented as an exact reproduction. Hydroxylamine availability is a feedstock gap; residual hydroxylamine could outcompete ammonia during acyl activation and form hydroxamates. No selective removal or integrated glutamine production has been demonstrated.

reactions.name: Aluminium-assisted transamination from glycine

conditions.catalyst: Al(III) supplied as potassium aluminium sulfate
conditions.other: Reported benchmark: pH 5, 350 mM glycine, alpha-ketoglutarate at 1.2 equivalents and alum at 0.1 equivalent, for 4 h. This corresponds to approximately 420 mM alpha-ketoglutarate and 35 mM alum relative to the stated glycine concentration. Cool by shallow shaded runoff before activation tests. Excess glycine and dissolved aluminium are not assumed removed.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_019 + mol_024 -> mol_020 + mol_016. Metal-assisted imine chemistry transfers the amino group from glycine to alpha-ketoglutarate, releasing glyoxylate.
reactions.reasoning: The supplied account of Stubbs et al. (2020) reports glutamate formation under these concentrated, alum-assisted transamination conditions. The amino-group transfer is not metal-free, even though a separate carbon-skeleton network in that work is. Aluminium availability at the required concentration is local and uncertain. Excess glycine is a serious competing nucleophile in either downstream activation module; no natural glutamate/glycine separation is established.

reactions.name: Speculative gamma-carboxyl activation by acetyl phosphate

conditions.other: Unvalidated screen: 10 mM glutamate, 10-50 mM acetyl phosphate, pH 6.5-7.5, UV-shielded water, sampling from 1 min to 24 h. Initially omit added ammonia to characterize activation. Determine alpha versus gamma activation, N-acetylation, hydrolysis and cyclization directly. No validated catalyst or selective mineral is known from the supplied literature.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_020 + mol_025 -> mol_027 + mol_026. Proposed attack of the gamma-carboxylate at phosphorus transfers a phosphoryl group and releases acetate. The nominated product has connectivity HOOC-CH(NH2)-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-O-P(=O)(OH)2.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE. No supplied paper demonstrates selective, enzyme-free gamma-glutamyl phosphate formation from glutamate and acetyl phosphate. Acetyl phosphate's activation potential does not establish the rate or regioselectivity of this transfer. Biological gamma-carboxyl activation provides only a mechanistic analogy, not validation of this donor or free-solution implementation (Curnow et al., 1997; Oshikane et al., 2006). Alpha activation, N-acetylation and donor hydrolysis must be tested. This is a decisive bottleneck, not an established productive edge.

reactions.name: Conditional ammonolysis of gamma-glutamyl phosphate

conditions.other: Unvalidated enzyme-free screen: pH 7-7.5, 100 mM total ammonia/ammonium, UV shielding, sampling from seconds to 24 h. Approximate free NH3 is only 0.56-1.75 mM at pKa 9.25. Use a measured gamma-glutamyl phosphate input, not an assumed quantitative output from rxn_012. Quantify phosphate, pyroglutamate and regenerated glutamate.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_027 + mol_003 -> mol_031 + mol_028. Ammonia attacks the activated gamma-carbonyl, and phosphate leaves.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE as a prebiotic free-solution reaction. Ammonolysis of an acyl phosphate is chemically credible conditional on intermediate availability, and activated gamma-glutamyl chemistry has biochemical precedent (Curnow et al., 1997; Oshikane et al., 2006). Those studies do not establish this enzyme-free reaction, its rate, or its competition with hydrolysis and intramolecular lactam formation. Glutamine stability constraints motivate the cool pH window but do not prove synthesis (Arii et al., 1999).

reactions.name: Speculative cyanamide-associated gamma-carboxyl activation

conditions.other: Unvalidated mechanistic screen: 10 mM glutamate, 0.1 M cyanamide, pH 5.5-6.5, UV-shielded water, 1 min to 24 h. No effective catalyst is established. Detect or exclude the proposed activated intermediate before interpreting any amide signal; monitor cyanamide hydrolysis, oligomerization and alpha-carboxyl activation.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_020 + mol_029 -> mol_037. A proposed carbodiimide-tautomer-mediated addition gives an O-acylisourea with connectivity HOOC-CH(NH2)-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-O-C(=NH)-NH2. Formation of this species from cyanamide under these conditions is not established.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE, with no direct supporting experiment in the supplied literature. This makes explicit the activation hypothesis rather than treating cyanamide-to-urea conversion as proof of amidation. The reactive tautomer may be too scarce, and water or other nucleophiles may dominate. There is no evidence for gamma selectivity. It is retained only as a chemically distinct, falsifiable activator experiment, not as an effective prebiotic condensing system.

reactions.name: Conditional ammonolysis of the proposed gamma-O-acylisourea

conditions.other: Unvalidated screen: pH 7-7.5, 100 mM total ammonia/ammonium, protected from UV, sampled from seconds to 24 h. Free NH3 is approximately 0.56-1.75 mM. Requires demonstrated availability of mol_037. Quantify glutamine, isoglutamine, pyroglutamate, glutamate and urea; residual glycine or hydroxylamine must be included in compatibility controls.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_037 + mol_003 -> mol_031 + mol_030. Ammonia attacks the gamma-acyl carbonyl of the proposed activated ester, releasing a urea-forming leaving group.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE, without a glutamine-forming demonstration in the supplied literature. General acyl-substitution logic supports this conditional mechanism, not the formation or selectivity of its precursor. Hydrolysis, intramolecular cyclization and rearrangement to unreactive acylureas may dominate. The cool pH window follows product-stability evidence, not demonstrated activation or ammonolysis kinetics (Arii et al., 1999).

reactions.name: Speculative alpha-nitrile hydrolysis while retaining the side-chain nitrile

conditions.other: Unvalidated selectivity screen: 1-10 mM aminodinitrile, pH 8.5-10, UV shielding, sampling over 0.25-14 days. No substrate-specific selective catalyst is known. Identify both amide and acid intermediates. Before rxn_017, cool to at most 303 K and adjust to pH 6.5-7.5 by buffered mixing; quantify dilution and carryover.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_014 + 2 mol_005 -> mol_032 + mol_003. The alpha-nitrile would have to pass through its amide to a carboxylate while the terminal nitrile remains intact, giving HOOC-CH(NH2)-CH2-CH2-CN.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE. Green et al. (2023) found differential nitrile hydration in related N-formyl substrates, including faster alpha-nitrile hydration, but did not demonstrate this unprotected C5 conversion. Faster hydration to an alpha-amide does not establish complete alpha-hydrolysis with retention of the other nitrile. Patel et al. (2015) provide only the starting aminodinitrile. Rates, acid-versus-amide selectivity and cyclization must be measured.

reactions.name: Speculative selective hydration of the side-chain nitrile to glutamine

conditions.other: Unvalidated screen: 1-10 mM gamma-cyano amino acid, pH 6.5-7.5, UV shielding, sampling from 1 h to 7 days. No compatible selective catalyst is identified in the supplied literature. Uncatalysed hydration may be too slow to compete with product loss; no useful rate is assumed.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_032 + mol_005 -> mol_031. Hydration of the remaining nitrile would produce the gamma-amide while retaining the existing alpha-carboxylate.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE and a decisive target-forming bottleneck. Green et al. (2023) provide only substrate-dependent analogue chemistry, not this reaction. Neither rate enhancement nor stopping at the amide has been demonstrated under glutamine-compatible conditions. Over-hydrolysis through rxn_022 remains possible. A cool environment aids persistence but does not make nitrile hydration kinetically competent (Arii et al., 1999).

reactions.name: Low-priority speculative side-chain-first nitrile hydration

conditions.other: Unvalidated control screen: 1-10 mM aminodinitrile, pH 7-9, UV shielding, sampled over 1 h to 14 days. No selective catalyst or productive residence time is known. A positive assignment must distinguish this gamma-amide/alpha-nitrile from the isomeric alpha-amide/gamma-nitrile.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_014 + mol_005 -> mol_033. Only the terminal nitrile would hydrate, yielding NC-CH(NH2)-CH2-CH2-CONH2 while preserving the alpha-aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE and lower priority than testing alpha-first reactivity. The analogue results of Green et al. (2023) do not support assuming preferential side-chain hydration; they instead caution that the alpha-nitrile can react first. Patel et al. (2015) did not perform this conversion. The node records a testable alternative product branch, not an endorsed regioselective synthesis.

reactions.name: Speculative alpha-nitrile hydrolysis with gamma-amide retention

conditions.other: Unvalidated screen: pH 6.5-7.5, UV-shielded water, sampling over 1 h to 7 days. Requires a structurally confirmed mol_033 input. No catalyst is known to complete alpha-nitrile hydrolysis while preserving the side-chain amide under this window. Hot acid is excluded because it would undermine the required selectivity.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_033 + 2 mol_005 -> mol_031 + mol_003. Complete hydrolysis of the alpha-nitrile would give the alpha-carboxylate while leaving the gamma-amide intact.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE, with no direct support in the supplied research. This requires a second unestablished selectivity after rxn_018, and an alpha-amide intermediate may accumulate instead. Analogue nitrile hydration does not validate complete alpha-hydrolysis (Green et al., 2023). The temperature and pH restrictions are imposed by glutamine persistence, not by evidence that this reaction proceeds there (Arii et al., 1999).

reactions.name: Competing differential hydrolysis to isoglutamine

conditions.other: Competing-product screen across pH 7-10, 1-10 mM aminodinitrile and 1 h to 14 days. No product ratio or rate is established. Use authentic glutamine and isoglutamine standards; exact mass alone cannot distinguish them.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_014 + 3 mol_005 -> mol_034 + mol_003. The alpha-nitrile stops at an amide while the side-chain nitrile proceeds to the acid, giving HOOC-CH2-CH2-CH(NH2)-CONH2.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE as a substrate-specific branch, but chemically necessary to consider when interpreting differential nitrile hydrolysis. Green et al. (2023) demonstrate that related dinitriles have unequal hydration behaviour without establishing the desired C5 product. The tentative glutamine mass assignment in tholin hydrolysates cannot exclude this constitutional isomer (Neish et al., 2010). No demonstrated isoglutamine selectivity is claimed either.

reactions.name: Measured glutamine-loss pathway: cyclization to pyroglutamate

conditions.other: Reference: pH 7.2 and approximately 10% loss per day at 310.15 K. First-order conversion gives k approximately 0.105 day^-1, or 1.22e-6 s^-1, and half-life approximately 6.6 days. These are condition-specific values. Shielding from UV does not suppress this spontaneous loss.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_031 -> mol_035 + mol_003. Intramolecular attack of the alpha-amino group on the gamma-amide produces a five-membered lactam and releases ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Supported by Tritsch and Moore (1962) and Arii et al. (1999). The cited studies give different apparent activation energies, approximately 48.5 and 98.7 kJ/mol under different conditions; they should not be treated as a single fitted kinetic model. Any Arrhenius extrapolation must be labelled an estimate. Net accumulation requires J_production greater than the combined cyclization, hydrolysis and export losses; no productive flux is available for the proposed synthesis edges.

reactions.name: Competing glutamine deamidation to glutamate

conditions.temperature: 300-370 K; loss-characterization range, not a synthesis window
conditions.other: Measure separately at the intended pH 5-7.5 storage conditions and during accidental thermal or acid/base exposure. No independent cool-water hydrolysis constant is provided by the supplied research. Do not assign the cyclization rate from rxn_021 to this separate reaction.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_031 + mol_005 -> mol_020 + mol_003. Side-chain amide hydrolysis releases ammonia and regenerates glutamate.
reactions.reasoning: Glutamine conversion to glutamate under heating and processing is supported by Airaudo et al. (1987). The importance of this branch relative to direct lactam formation depends on temperature, pH and solution composition. It is included as a loss and analytical-workup hazard, not assigned a rapid rate in cool neutral water.

reactions.name: Thermal or dehydrating glutamate cyclization

conditions.other: Concentrated films undergoing partial drying, with exposure measured over hours to days. This is not assigned as a rapid reaction in cool dilute water. Conversion at this relatively mild temperature range must be measured rather than inferred from much hotter decomposition experiments.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_020 -> mol_035 + mol_005. Intramolecular lactamization eliminates water from glutamate.
reactions.reasoning: Gayte-Sorbier et al. (1985) report that heating glutamate gives pyroglutamate rather than glutamine. Weiss et al. (2018) examine substantially hotter thermal decomposition, not the rate at 350-370 K. The branch cautions against treating wet-dry heating as a glutamine-forming process; its low-temperature kinetics remain unspecified.

reactions.name: Competing hydrolysis of gamma-glutamyl phosphate

conditions.other: Same pH 6.5-7.5 matrix as the activation and ammonolysis tests; sample from seconds to 24 h. Determine the hydrolysis constant independently, with and without ammonia and with measured metal carryover. No half-life is supplied or assumed.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_027 + mol_005 -> mol_020 + mol_028. Water cleaves the acyl-phosphate linkage and regenerates glutamate.
reactions.reasoning: Chemically expected for an activated acyl phosphate, but its rate in this proposed free gamma-glutamyl phosphate system is not established by the supplied literature. Biological use of activated gamma-glutamyl intermediates does not provide an abiotic lifetime (Curnow et al., 1997; Oshikane et al., 2006). This conditional loss must compete explicitly with rxn_013.

reactions.name: Competing lactamization of gamma-glutamyl phosphate

conditions.other: pH 6.5-7.5, seconds-to-hours sampling following any detected activation. Compare with ammonia trapping and hydrolysis under identical conditions. The alpha-amino group is largely protonated, but no protective effect sufficient to prevent intramolecular reaction is assumed.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_027 -> mol_035 + mol_028. The alpha-amino group attacks the activated gamma-carbonyl intramolecularly, forming a five-membered lactam and expelling phosphate.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE in rate and magnitude for this free activated intermediate, but mechanistically credible and essential to test. The known stability of the pyroglutamate sink does not establish a measured rate for its formation from gamma-glutamyl phosphate (Arii et al., 1999). Enzyme-bound biochemical intermediates cannot be used to infer protection of the free compound.

reactions.name: Competing speculative alpha-carboxyl activation

conditions.other: Use the same unvalidated 10 mM glutamate, 10-50 mM acetyl phosphate and pH 6.5-7.5 screen as rxn_012. Determine positional activation directly. No alpha-to-gamma activation ratio is assigned.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_020 + mol_025 -> mol_036 + mol_026. Competing phosphoryl transfer at the alpha-carboxylate would form HOOC-CH2-CH2-CH(NH2)-C(=O)-O-P(=O)(OH)2.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE, without direct support in the supplied literature. This branch prevents the graph from silently assuming gamma specificity for a molecule containing two carboxyl groups. Biochemical specificity depends on organized catalysts and is not evidence for regioselective free-solution activation (Curnow et al., 1997; Oshikane et al., 2006). Both proposed acyl phosphates could be absent if competing donor reactions dominate.

reactions.name: Conditional alpha-acyl-phosphate ammonolysis to isoglutamine

conditions.other: Unvalidated pH 7-7.5 screen with 100 mM total ammonia/ammonium; seconds-to-hours sampling. Requires verified alpha-glutamyl phosphate. Resolve isoglutamine from glutamine chromatographically and, where possible, by structure-specific spectroscopy.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_036 + mol_003 -> mol_034 + mol_028. Ammonolysis of the activated alpha-carboxyl group yields the alpha-amide, not glutamine.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE as a demonstrated reaction in this setting, but chemically plausible if the nominated intermediate forms. This competing branch makes the constitutional-isomer problem explicit. The tentative mass-spectrometric glutamine assignment of Neish et al. (2010) cannot establish this or the desired regioisomer because their elemental formulas are identical.

reactions.name: Competing hydrolysis of the proposed gamma-O-acylisourea

conditions.other: Same pH 5.5-7.5 range used for the cyanamide activation/ammonolysis screens. Sample from seconds to 24 h. Measure water-driven loss separately from rearrangement and cyclization; no intermediate lifetime is known.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_037 + mol_005 -> mol_020 + mol_030. Hydrolysis of the proposed activated ester regenerates glutamate and produces urea.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE because the intermediate itself has not been demonstrated in the supplied research. Hydrolysis is a chemically credible competitor for an O-acylisourea. Observing urea alone would not establish glutamine production, since this loss gives the same activator-derived product without amidation. No source-specific rate or yield can be assigned.

reactions.name: Competing cyclization of the proposed gamma-O-acylisourea

conditions.other: pH 5.5-7.5, sampled from seconds to 24 h under the same matrix as rxn_015. Determine cyclization relative to ammonia trapping, hydrolysis and acylurea rearrangement. No branching fraction is assumed.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced candidate equation: mol_037 -> mol_035 + mol_030. Intramolecular alpha-amino attack on the activated gamma-carbonyl forms pyroglutamate and releases a urea-forming leaving group.
reactions.reasoning: SPECULATIVE for this unobserved intermediate. Five-membered lactam formation is chemically plausible, and known glutamine/glutamate loss chemistry makes it a necessary competitor to test rather than ignore (Gayte-Sorbier et al., 1985; Arii et al., 1999). Those papers do not measure this activated-intermediate reaction, so its kinetics remain unknown.

reactions.name: Competing hydrolysis of alpha-glutamyl phosphate

conditions.other: pH 6.5-7.5, seconds-to-hours sampling, with matched ammonia-free controls. No alpha-acyl-phosphate lifetime or comparison with gamma-acyl-phosphate stability is established.

reactions.mechanism: Balanced net equation: mol_036 + mol_005 -> mol_020 + mol_028. Hydrolytic cleavage regenerates glutamate and orthophosphate.
reactions.reasoning: Chemically expected conditional on formation of the proposed alpha-acyl phosphate, but not directly supported by a substrate-specific experiment in the supplied literature. This prevents all alpha activation from being counted automatically as isoglutamine formation. Both productive and nonproductive acyl-phosphate fates need measured kinetics.

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic glutamate supply followed by candidate acyl-phosphate amidation
pathways.description: Supported aminodinitrile formation is followed by conditional complete hydrolysis to glutamate, speculative gamma-phosphorylation and conditional ammonolysis. Hot-acid workup requires cooling and neutralization. The decisive activation and selectivity gaps remain open.

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic glutamate supply followed by candidate cyanamide-associated amidation
pathways.description: Uses the same precursor chemistry as P1 but tests a chemically different, unvalidated activation hypothesis. Formation of the proposed O-acylisourea must be established before its ammonolysis can be considered productive.

pathways.name: Hydrogen/nickel glutamate supply followed by candidate acyl-phosphate amidation
pathways.description: Hydrogen-driven ketoacid assembly and nickel-catalysed reductive amination supply glutamate. Removal of nickel solids does not establish removal of dissolved metals. The final enzyme-free gamma-activation/ammonolysis module is unvalidated.

pathways.name: Hydrogen/nickel glutamate supply followed by candidate cyanamide-associated amidation
pathways.description: Shares experimentally supported glutamate-supply chemistry with P3 but tests the proposed O-acylisourea mechanism. Neither cyanamide-mediated activation nor gamma selectivity has been demonstrated.

pathways.name: Iron/hydroxylamine glutamate supply followed by candidate acyl-phosphate amidation
pathways.description: Uses hydrogen-driven carbon-skeleton assembly followed by a chemically distinct iron/hydroxylamine nitrogen-introduction module. Cooling and residual-hydroxylamine analysis are required. The terminal gamma-activation step remains speculative.

pathways.name: Iron/hydroxylamine glutamate supply followed by candidate cyanamide-associated amidation
pathways.description: Combines the iron/hydroxylamine glutamate branch with the speculative O-acylisourea branch. Residual hydroxylamine could divert activated glutamate to hydroxamates, so this is not an established compatible cascade.

pathways.name: Glycine transamination followed by candidate acyl-phosphate amidation
pathways.description: Hydrogen-driven ketoacid assembly supplies alpha-ketoglutarate for alum-assisted transamination. The carbon assembly is not labelled metal-free. Concentrated glycine and aluminium carryover create unresolved competition during speculative gamma-activation.

pathways.name: Glycine transamination followed by candidate cyanamide-associated amidation
pathways.description: Uses the transamination glutamate supply and tests cyanamide-associated activation. No selective glutamate/glycine separation is assumed; competing peptide formation and other nucleophile trapping must be quantified. Glutamine production remains unvalidated.

pathways.name: Aminodinitrile hydrolysis with alpha-acid formation first
pathways.description: Tests complete alpha-nitrile hydrolysis with side-chain nitrile retention, followed by side-chain hydration. Related N-formyl-substrate evidence motivates testing differential reactivity but validates neither selective step in the unprotected C5 substrate. No overall yield or useful hydration rate is known.

pathways.name: Low-priority aminodinitrile hydrolysis with gamma-amide formation first
pathways.description: Tests side-chain-first hydration followed by complete alpha-nitrile hydrolysis. Both selectivities are unestablished, and the first is not favoured by the cited analogue evidence. This is a falsifiable alternative sequence, not a tenth demonstrated or equally credible prebiotic synthesis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Patel et al. (2015) supports rxn_001 through rxn_006, not production of free glutamine. Complete hydrolysis in rxn_007 is plausible but needs specified conditions and demonstrated glutamate recovery. The decisive gap is rxn_012: acetyl phosphate is not established to selectively phosphorylate glutamate's gamma-carboxylate. Hydrolysis, acetyl transfer and alpha-carboxyl activation are competing possibilities. Ammonolysis in rxn_013 is chemically plausible conditional on gamma-glutamyl phosphate formation, but its competition with hydrolysis and intramolecular lactamization is unmeasured.
suggestions: Specify and validate the complete-hydrolysis workup, glutamate recovery, and dissolved copper/sulfide carryover into the activation module.
Measure gamma- versus alpha-glutamyl phosphate formation, acetylated products, glutamine, isoglutamine and pyroglutamate in a time-resolved activation/ammonolysis experiment.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The precursor sequence has substantial support from Patel et al. (2015), but neither cyanamide-mediated gamma activation nor subsequent glutamine production is established. Cyanamide cannot simply be assumed to behave like an effective carbodiimide coupling reagent in cool, near-neutral water. Formation, gamma selectivity and lifetime of mol_037 are unverified. Its proposed ammonolysis is plausible only conditionally, while hydrolysis, lactamization and possible rearrangement can consume the activated species.
suggestions: Establish whether mol_037 actually forms under the proposed conditions using structural evidence rather than urea production alone.
Resolve alpha versus gamma activation and measure ammonolysis against hydrolysis, lactamization and possible acylurea formation before integrating the upstream module.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the strongest relative candidate because Kaur et al. (2024) supports the H2/Ni precursor chemistry under comparatively mild conditions, while ammonolysis of a preformed gamma-acyl phosphate has a reasonable mechanistic basis. Nevertheless, rxn_012 remains unvalidated and prevents a high-confidence route to glutamine. At pH 5-7.5, most ammoniacal nitrogen is protonated; the available NH3 concentration and competition with lactamization must be measured. Nickel phase, H2 pressure and downstream carryover are not adequately specified by the environment label.
suggestions: Provide reaction-specific nickel phase, loading, H2 pressure, pH, residence time and glutamate recovery, with a citation mapping for rxn_008 and rxn_009.
First validate gamma-glutamyl phosphate formation and NH3 capture with purified glutamate, then repeat using the actual precursor-module effluent and quantify net glutamine accumulation.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Kaur et al. (2024) provides a credible glutamate-supply module but does not support the cyanamide activation step. The balanced equation for rxn_014 establishes conservation, not formation of the proposed O-acylisourea or its gamma regioselectivity. Even if mol_037 forms, ammonia capture must outcompete hydrolysis and cyclization. Mild precursor conditions help compatibility but do not resolve this central chemical uncertainty.
suggestions: Directly characterize the proposed activated intermediate and establish its formation rate, regioselectivity and lifetime in the specified aqueous medium.
Test precursor-effluent compatibility and perform an isotopically traced ammonia-capture experiment with authentic glutamine and isoglutamine standards.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Muchowska et al. (2019) supports iron/hydroxylamine chemistry leading to glutamate under specified heated, inert conditions. The supplied balance correctly treats iron as a consumed reductant. This pathway also retains the requirements of the upstream H2-dependent rxn_008. Cooling and settling are sensible, but residual hydroxylamine can intercept activated carboxyl groups as hydroxamates, and dissolved iron is not necessarily removed by settling. Gamma phosphorylation and productive ammonolysis remain unvalidated.
suggestions: Measure residual hydroxylamine, dissolved iron, glutamate recovery and competing hydroxamate formation after the proposed transfer.
Demonstrate that rxn_012 and rxn_013 operate in the transferred mixture faster than activated-intermediate hydrolysis and cyclization.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The iron/hydroxylamine glutamate-supply step is literature-guided, but the pathway still depends on rxn_008 and its distinct requirements. Cyanamide-mediated formation of mol_037 is the principal unsupported transformation. Residual hydroxylamine adds an important competing nucleophile during any successful carboxyl activation. Separating mineral solids and cooling the stream do not establish removal of this dissolved competitor or demonstrate glutamine production.
suggestions: Validate mol_037 formation and ammonia capture independently before combining the cyanamide and iron/hydroxylamine modules.
Quantify hydroxylamine carryover and compare glutamine, hydroxamates, glutamate and pyroglutamate in integrated versus purified-substrate experiments.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The aluminium-assisted glycine transamination is supported by the supplied Stubbs et al. (2020) findings under concentrated, heated conditions. The graph still uses the H2-dependent rxn_008 for alpha-ketoglutarate supply. Aluminium speciation, cooling and transfer recovery need specification. Substantial residual glycine could compete with ammonia for activated glutamate, producing peptide products rather than glutamine. The unproven gamma-phosphorylation step remains decisive.
suggestions: Specify the aluminium source and speciation, glycine concentration, temperature and downstream carryover corresponding to the demonstrated transamination.
Measure glutamine formation against glycine capture, alpha amidation, hydrolysis and pyroglutamate formation using the actual cooled transamination mixture.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The transamination module has experimental precedent, whereas cyanamide-associated gamma activation does not. High residual glycine introduces competition for any activated glutamyl intermediate, while alpha activation and lactamization remain unresolved. The supplied cooling and separation plan avoids assuming glutamine survives the heated precursor stage, but does not establish sufficient purification or selective ammonia capture in the final mixture.
suggestions: Determine whether cyanamide produces the proposed gamma intermediate rather than other activated, rearranged or condensed products.
Compare purified glutamate with unpurified transamination effluent and quantify glycine-containing products alongside glutamine, isoglutamine and pyroglutamate.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Patel et al. (2015) supports production of the aminodinitrile, but not rxn_016 or rxn_017. Green et al. (2023) studied protected, shorter-chain analogues under different conditions; those results do not establish selective alpha-acid formation for this unprotected C5 substrate. Subsequent side-chain nitrile hydration must have a useful rate while stopping at the amide. No catalyst or kinetic evidence establishes either requirement in the proposed cool pH 5-7.5 water. Isoglutamine formation in rxn_020 is also an unmeasured possibility, not a demonstrated product distribution.
suggestions: Measure time-resolved hydrolysis of authentic mol_014, resolving both nitrile sites, intermediate amides, mol_032, glutamine, isoglutamine and glutamate.
Identify a condition or catalyst that hydrates mol_032 at the proposed temperature and pH, and show that glutamine production exceeds further hydrolysis and cyclization losses.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The network correctly labels this as low priority. The supplied Green et al. (2023) analogue evidence favors initial alpha-nitrile reaction rather than the side-chain-first selectivity required by rxn_018, although differences in substrate and conditions prevent treating this as a definitive disproof. Reaction rxn_019 additionally requires complete alpha-nitrile hydrolysis while retaining the gamma-amide. Neither selectivity nor adequate reaction rates have been established in the proposed final environment.
suggestions: Require direct detection and structural assignment of mol_033 before treating the side-chain-first sequence as an operative route.
Determine both nitrile-site reaction rates and test mol_033 separately for alpha-acid formation, gamma-amide retention and competing cyclization.

evaluation.network_feedback: Not approved at the network threshold of 0.90. Structural validity is high: the 37 molecule nodes and 30 reaction nodes form a connected network with consistent IDs, and the authoritative balance check reports no atom or charge conservation violations. The coefficients of eight in rxn_003 and rxn_004 reflect the S8 representation and are not problematic. Literature alignment is strong in the hypothesis framing: supported precursor chemistry is distinguished from unvalidated target-forming chemistry, glutamine is distinguished from isoglutamine, and loss pathways and analytical artifacts are acknowledged. However, the supplied reaction summaries lack explicit reaction-level citations and most quantitative conditions. Every productive route encounters a decisive unresolved transformation: rxn_012 or rxn_014 in P1-P8, or selective nitrile hydrolysis in P9-P10. Neither balanced equations nor biochemical precedent establishes useful abiotic glutamine production. The known losses in rxn_021-rxn_023 and plausible activated-intermediate sinks in rxn_024-rxn_030 can prevent accumulation; their rates in the proposed mixtures remain unmeasured. Cooling, shielding and separate pools are sensible provisions, but Surface and Biochemical are insufficient physical specifications, and settling does not establish removal of dissolved metals or competing nucleophiles. Boundary feedstocks are accepted as inputs rather than treated as missing synthesis steps, although required concentrations and transfer recoveries still need environmental justification. Reaction scores include relevant competing branches; high loss-reaction scores indicate plausible losses, not credit toward target production. Overall confidence is limited by unresolved target-forming chemistry, not averaged upward by precursor reactions, pathway counts or shared intermediates. P3 is the strongest relative experimental candidate, not a validated synthesis. The network is useful as a research plan, but demonstrating free glutamine requires structural confirmation, quantified selectivity, realistic mixture-transfer tests, and measured production exceeding chemical and transport losses.
